body:
Although the way this space adventure is written and filmed keeps you enraptured with the plot and sense of adventure, it is easy to forget that Ryan Gosling spends most of his time acting alone, and he deserves much credit for his seamless performance. Apparently, no green screen was used during the filming with a set built for the spaceship interior and an animatronic or puppet used for Rocky, with SFX added to enhance it afterwards.

Based on Andy Weir's second novel, it has some similarities in structure to The Martian, in that a lone Spaceman must use science and his wits to save himself, and in this case, both humanity and his newfound friend, an Alien called Rocky. What is so enjoyable about this film is not the sense of looming disaster but rather the story about how two species meeting for the first time in the vastness of space learn to communicate, work together to solve the riddle of dying stars and to eventually become friends. It is a smart mix of tension and heartfelt adventure. It is the kind of film I can say is a departure from the formulaic expectations we might have from sci-fi disaster movies. So much is so good here that, for pure entertainment value, it is difficult to fault and I already want to watch it again.

Very much like many other films that came before it, when faced with ineluctable demise, Earth sends its best and brightest scientist hurtling through the cosmos in search of an answer to avoid its impending doom. Well... maybe not the best. I never read the book, but Project Hail Mary has been on my radar since the first trailer dropped.

There were hints of comedic elements in the film, but what I wasn't expecting was for it to be a buddy sci-fi comedy with heartfelt moments that really stick with you.

Space on its own is terrifying enough: the instant freezing temperatures if exposed, the complete absence of gravity, debris from the far corners of the galaxy, etc. These are only a few examples of the many threats one would face while exploring the final frontier. But the real challenge is the loneliness-the complete void of space where there is no up nor down. Just Dr. Ryland Grace, a middle school science teacher portrayed by Ryan Gosling, with literally the fate of the world riding on his shoulders, all by his lonesome.

Until he meets another traveler, whom he names Rocky, given his distinct features.

It's rare for me to see a film that hits me in the feels and demands a genuine emotional response. Watching the duo coexist, develop a form of communication, and work together to achieve a singular goal is something that works incredibly well in the film.

In the infinite vacuum of space, the two lonely astronauts find each other and share experiences ranging from frustration to jokes to puppeteered figures, showcasing to audiences that the relationship between the two characters feels real-something even admirable.

So yeah, get your tissues ready.

There's a lot of beautiful imagery throughout the film, complemented by some well-done editing. The runtime might be a bit much for some, but in my personal experience the story is so engaging that audiences will barely notice it. All the jokes and gimmicks land beautifully, Ryan Gosling is fantastic, and though we've seen similar stories before, it somehow still feels fresh. It also knows exactly how to pull on the heartstrings of its viewers by focusing on some heavy themes that remove audiences from their seats and place them on the vessel, asking the same questions as our lead.

All in all, this is a great piece of cinema that takes us on a voyage in search of answers while discovering friendship in dark and unsuspecting places.

I saw a pre-release showing in Dolby Cinema. It was incredible. While it had to streamline a lot of the science in the book, this is as good of an adaptation as one could possibly hope for. The breathtaking cinematography by Greig Fraser and fantastic performance by Ryan Gosling cement it as one of the sci-fi greats.

Not if Ken and a weird rock creature have anything to say about that!

Yeah I've pretty much become numb to science fiction stories nowadays, and personally I blame the Star Wars franchise for that. How are we supposed to care about plots that represent the inherent humanity of characters when they're stuck inside such generic, contrived takes on what should be fantastical worlds beyond imagination??

That's where Project Hail Mary shines, because it is a deeply human story that embraces the flaws of human error, biology, loneliness and mortality that just so happens to have sci-fi elements. Perhaps it runs maybe 20 minutes too long and there are a few eye-rolling moments, but the movie compensates for that with some of the greatest cinematography I've witnessed on the big screen in a hot minute, to the point where the camera is easily its own character.

Lord and Miller got to make their own Han Solo film after all. There is hope yet for the world.

I rarely write reviews on this site. But as this is an adaptation of one of my favorite novels of recent times, this was necessary.

Being a Big fan of the novel (reading the book 3 times), and one of my favorite novels of all time, What can I say? A masterpiece of adaptation. With a talented screenwriter like Drew Goddard adapting the work and talented directors like Lord and Miller, I already imagined it would be at least great.

Ryan Gosling was perfect in the role. This film will be nominated for several awards, it will be nominated for several Oscars, and Gosling will probably be nominated for best actor.

Ther score of Daniel Pemberton (Spiderverse 1 2 3) is sublime, like a Vangelis score type, Greig Fraser (Dune parts 1 2) Cinematography it´s top notch, Charles Wood Design (from many MCU films) it´s out of this World. The effects are perfect, but for a certain character most of them (for the happyness of me and many fans ) they are made of practical effects and I always thought that was the right way to create them. Who read or watched the movie knows who I am talking about.

Of course like in every adaptation, some things are removed, like some characters and scenes, but the main plot of course is here, and is faithful.

This is a great year for sci-fi fans. Project Hail Mary adaptation, Disclosure Day from Spielberg (his return to directing aliens), Dune Part 3 from Villeneuve.

I feel that Project Hail Mary will be one of the films with the most Oscar nominations in 2027, along with Christopher Nolan's Odyssey. But I hope it's time for the first alien and space film to win best picture, director, and screenplay.
